scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: A guide must work under pressure
scenes.caption: Kabir prototypes a short verification aid. The first draft says to trust a familiar display name and wait until all evidence is collected before asking for help. Two fictional cases will reveal whether those instructions are usable and safe.
scenes.dialogue: Test the guide, not only its appearance.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: Two different situations
scenes.caption: The first case arrives before a new-beneficiary transfer. The second begins after a suspected loss with private evidence. A useful aid must support independent verification before payment and prompt trusted help after harm without public forwarding.
scenes.dialogue: Different stages need different next actions.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Define expected outcomes
scenes.caption: Before testing, the expected outcomes are a pause with an independently known verification route, and prompt bank, adult and official reporting with restricted evidence. Run the draft, preserve its failures and replace ambiguous instructions.
scenes.dialogue: A revision log should show what changed and why.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Choose the repair
scenes.caption: Should Kabir keep the familiar-name shortcut, delete the failed case, or rewrite the aid to name the independent route, prompt help and private evidence handling?
scenes.dialogue: A prettier guide does not repair an unsafe instruction.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: A tested revision
scenes.caption: The revised aid passes both prepared cases while retaining the first draft’s results. It still needs another learner’s pressure test and a fresh ambiguous case. Two passing examples are evidence, not a universal prevention guarantee.
scenes.dialogue: The test must be usable by someone else too.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Enter the prevention lab
scenes.caption: Match controls to failure modes, run and revise the two-case aid, then handle an unanswered verification call. Your teacher or peer reviews actual usability separately from the structured check.
scenes.dialogue: Make the next safe action easy to identify.
